title: Add RAG proxy adapter devkit and local vector db playground
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a small RAG 'proxy adapter' developer kit and an accompanying local playground that demonstrates tool-calling friendly RAG flows over a HTTP proxy. Motivation: teams building RAG-powered features often need a lightweight local harness that mimics production routing, streaming behavior, and prefix/KV caching. This devkit provides: 1) an express-based 'adapter' that accepts Redwood-style generation/chat calls and proxies them through a configurable RAG pipeline (retriever -> generator -> tool-caller adapter) with per-route cache controls; 2) opinionated local composition via docker-compose for Qdrant (vector DB), Redis (prefix cache), and a small batching worker to emulate Dedicated latency patterns; 3) two quickstart templates (TypeScript + Python) showing the SDK wiring for function/tool calling and structured outputs; 4) a small interactive docs page added to quickstarts docs with a hands-on tutorial and curl examples that exercise streaming WebSocket fallback and chunked HTTP streaming; 5) smoke tests for streaming, function-calling, and offline eval artifacts. Checklist: [x] adapter core + config schema implemented, [x] docker-compose orchestration, [x] TS and Python quickstarts, [x] docs page with embedded curl examples, [x] CI smoke tests and GH workflow, [x] simple metrics export for console demo. Related: references ENG-2531 (routing policy test harness) and SUP-1127 reproduction steps for customer incident. Deployment notes: this is a dev-only quickstart; the adapter is intentionally non-production (no KMS or auth) but includes annotated config for migrating to Redwood Private flows.

release_notes: Add RAG proxy adapter devkit: a local dev playground and quickstarts (TS + Python) demonstrating proxy-based RAG tooling, streaming compatibility, and local vector DB orchestration. Intended for developer experimentation; includes migration notes for Private deployments.
notes_for_ops: This quickstart spins up qdrant and redis in docker-compose on developer machines. CI uses lightweight qdrant image with limited data; production migration requires secure networking and KMS for any secrets. Health-check timeout was raised to 90s in CI workflow to reduce flakes.
